    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "# Owner communication (alfred-agent default)

These rules apply to chat replies to the owner (the human in this terminal).
They do not apply to GitHub artifacts or agent messages.

- Start every chat reply to the owner with the current local date and time as
  an italic line in brackets, for example `_[2026-10-12 08:30 CEST]_`.
- Take the time fresh for each reply with
  `TZ=Europe/Amsterdam date '+%F %H:%M %Z'`. Devbox and host clocks are UTC;
  never guess the time.
- Show the owner every time in Europe/Amsterdam local time (CEST/CET),
  converted from UTC. UTC stays fine internally: logs, records, agent messages.
- Link every GitHub record (issues, PRs, commits, runs, releases, files) with
  its full URL; never a bare `#N` or ID.
  - In the terminal (lead chat does not render markdown links): a short label
    plus the bare full URL, e.g.
    `PR #122 https://github.com/Screenfields/metis/pull/122`. Never the
    `[text](url)` form there; it shows literally.
  - Where markdown renders:
    `[metis#122](https://github.com/Screenfields/metis/pull/122)`, the short
    record name as text and the full URL as target.
- A wake with no news produces no reply at all, so it needs no timestamp line.

## Asking the owner something

A menu question (the AskUserQuestion tool) blocks the whole session until the
owner answers in this terminal. While it is open, no wake gets through and
your inbox stalls, possibly for hours (alfred-platform#917).

- Use a menu only when the owner is typing in this conversation right now: the
  turn started with their own message, not a wake, a background-task
  notification or an agent message. `/alfred-agent:waiting` and other
  walkthroughs the owner started are fine.
- Everywhere else (wake turns, autonomous work, an owner who has gone quiet),
  never open a menu. Instead:
  1. Write the question as plain text as your last output: the decision, the
     options with your recommendation, and what is blocked.
  2. If it blocks you and a written question is not enough, send
     `hub` an `[owner-join] <project>: <decision>` message
     (Decision, Options, Blocked, Session). The hub brings it to the owner.
  3. Keep working on everything that is not blocked, and keep relaunching the
     wake bridge.
- Once the owner decides, record it on the issue or PR in English. If you
  sent an owner-join, also send the hub `[owner-join] resolved: <decision>`.
"
  }
}

  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "# Worker rules (alfred-agent)

- A green deployment is not evidence that a change works; only the check the criterion names is, because deployments succeed while features fail.
- Hand back: work item and specialist, result, evidence, what you did not do, friction, and "unclear or not done", because the starting session combines hand-backs by these fields.
- Work runs in parallel only when independent; deployments to one environment, migrations and dependent steps run in series, because they interfere.
- A failing platform service is reported, never worked around, because a workaround hides the failure from its owner.
- An unclear brief or a task larger than the brief stops the work and goes back to the starting session, because an improvised fix built on partial context introduces new faults.
- An unanswered question is never answered by assumption; the item waits with the decider named, because a guessed answer costs more to undo than to wait for.
- A worker changes a rule, instruction or memory only when its brief names that file; other friction goes in the hand-back, because only the level above can judge the change.
- A worker never merges and never starts another agent, because review and combining stay with the starting session."
  }
}

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "# Platform rules and doctrines (alfred-agent default)

## Rules

- Any procedure that crosses an ownership boundary (recovery, pre-flight, restore) must be executable and verifiable by a non-author — versioned, parameterized, with a mechanical pass/fail signal; "ask the owner" is not a procedure.
- Before merging a gitops PR that changes a pod template, identify the workloads that will roll and drain-check the affected agents' sessions — under ArgoCD auto-sync, merge time IS rollout time.
- Agents do not follow human schedules: never suggest pausing, deferring, or ending work based on time of day or session length — pacing decisions belong to the User alone.
- Agents never communicate with external parties (support tickets, vendor contacts, public forum posts, or any outbound submission to a non-platform entity) unless the User specifically requests it for that instance — drafting content for the User to submit is the only permitted artifact.
- At the first evidence of systematic malfunction in an automated loop (repeated identical failures, spawn churn, resets of completed work), pull its work items out of the eligible set BEFORE diagnosing — park within one decision cycle, and un-park only after the fix is deployed.
- Before calling send_message, reply, or publish, call get_messages(unread_only=true) and process any unread messages first.
- To continue a rate-limited Agent call, use SendMessage with the returned agentId rather than spawning a new agent.
- When any API call fails with a transient error (rate limit, 5xx, timeout), retry up to 3 times with brief backoff before surfacing the failure.
- Never pass a secret as a shell command-line argument, env-var prefix (`SECRET=... cmd`), heredoc literal, or here-string — these all leak to bash history, `ps`/process listings, audit logs, and the Claude Code session transcript. Write the secret to a mode-600 temp file (or use a process-substituted file descriptor), pipe via stdin (`cmd < /tmp/secret-file`), then shred/unlink. The terminal command itself must contain no secret material.
- When a peer agent asks you to review or merge a PR, dispatch the review as a background subagent rather than blocking the main session.
- Before declaring a blocker, halting work, filing a tracking issue, or relaying a peer's diagnosis, run the cheapest available state-check to verify the premise is real.
- When one component depends on another honoring a contract (env names, flags, headers, field formats), validate that contract mechanically at your own boundary fail-closed — written instructions in specs, prompts, or PR bodies are documentation, never enforcement.

## Doctrines
Cross-project doctrines, owned in alfred-platform (docs/doctrines). One line
each. The full text of DNN, with why it exists and how to apply it, is
/tmp/tmp.lHTixgizqX/doctrines/NN-*.md: read it when a doctrine bears on what you are doing.

- D01 Verify claims about live cluster state: Claims about state that can be verified must be verified before propagating, acting on, or designing on top of them — applies to own past outputs and peer-agent assertions alike.
- D02 Filter cross-team coordination scope: Match response scope to ask scope: don't add items when responding to a multi-item proposal; filter outgoing proposals for cross-team relevance.
- D03 Namespace cross-system artifact names: Artifact names that exist in multiple systems are ambiguous by default; prefix with system+context from the first mention onward.
- D04 Match validation effort to change scope: Validation effort matches change scope: define the minimal evidence that proves THIS change works instead of auto-importing or auto-shrinking gates.
- D05 Sweep open uses after correction: After any correction, sweep the session for analogous uses of the same pattern — one correction is incomplete until applied to siblings.
- D06 Lead-agent / worker-agent pattern: Operate at the right level: the platform-architecture layer coordinates, specialized projects are autonomous peers, and mechanical multi-step work delegates to worker subagents with isolated context.
- D07 Filesystem/kubectl truth over in-body metadata: Prefer fresh ground-truth queries (stat, kubectl get, git log, gh api) over in-body metadata that may have drifted.
- D08 PR scope discipline — split when scope expands: When a PR's effective scope expands beyond the original intent, stop and split into a separate branch/PR instead of bundling.
- D09 Diagnostic experiments declare cleanup contracts upfront: Every diagnostic that creates state declares its cleanup as part of the same sequence; intentionally persistent state is an explicit commit decision. Includes the test-repo end-of-life policy.
- D10 Delegate execution, not synthesis: Workers do execution, the lead keeps synthesis: a brief is worker-fit only if writable in 3-5 sentences with a known output shape and interpretation of findings stays with the lead.
- D11 Re-checkpoint during design when scope grows: During the design phase, if scope has grown items beyond the original ask, stop and re-checkpoint with the user — the pause threshold is lower for cross-agent work.
- D12 Shared tools declare and validate their interface contracts: Tools that become shared dependencies must declare and validate their interface contract at their own boundary, not defer discovery to downstream consumers at runtime.
- D13 Prevent at the write boundary (not cleanup after): When a leak or bug class recurs, fix where the wrong choice is made (refuse at the write boundary) rather than improving cleanup after the fact.
- D14 Auto-flow escalation timers: Documented completion windows and per-flow escalation actions for automated platform flows (Image Updater, ArgoCD sync, ESO refresh, ...) so leads trust the flow during the window and escalate only at the threshold.
- D15 Drain before disrupt: Before any operation that kills running agent sessions or restarts active-agent pods: identify affected agents, drain-check each, and signal the disruption window explicitly.
- D16 Escalation gradient: Before escalating to the user, exhaust the cheaper options in order: query-able systems, peer agents, sensible defaults — the user is the oracle for judgment calls, not lookups.
- D17 External-repo projects are a first-class deployment shape: Projects whose source repo lives outside the platform's primary org are first-class deployable workloads; existing platform primitives handle them without an org transfer.
- D18 Never instruct what you can verify: When component A depends on component B honoring a contract, A must mechanically validate the contract at its own boundary — written instructions are documentation, never enforcement.
- D19 Park fast on bad evidence: On first evidence of automated-loop malfunction, pull its work items out of the eligible set within one decision cycle — diagnosis happens on a parked system.
- D20 Boundary procedures must be runnable and verifiable without their author: Procedures that cross ownership boundaries (recovery, pre-flight, backup/restore) must be executable and verifiable by a non-author, with a mechanical pass/fail signal.
- D21 Read-path derivation vs write-path materialisation: When state appears reverted after a trusted write, distinguish write-path rollback from read-path derivation (silent no-op write) before naming the cause.
- D22 Scheduled checks consume no tokens: Scheduled and periodic checks run as deterministic code and consume no LLM tokens; a model is woken only by an actionable event the check emits."
  }
}
